question: What is the final state of one liberated simultaneously with knowledge, regardless of place or memory at death?
premises: One may abandon the body at a holy place or in the house of a dog-cooker.
One may even have lost memory at the time of death.
One who is liberated simultaneously with knowledge goes to absolute isolation, free from sorrow.
inference: For one liberated in the very moment of knowledge, neither place nor memory at death affects the attainment of sorrowless absolute isolation.
plain_english: Whether at a holy place or in the house of a dog-cooker, even if memory is lost, one who abandons the body and is liberated simultaneously with knowledge goes to absolute isolation, with sorrow destroyed.
